content.text:
Yes. PR #2 (`automation/callisto-0.15.0`) rewrites `Formula/callisto.rb` in place, replacing every 0.14.2 URL and SHA with 0.15.0. The tap holds exactly one version per tool: the latest. The updater also refuses downgrades, so older versions can't be installed from the tap.

Homebrew's convention for this is versioned formulae, such as `Formula/callisto@0.14.rb` with `keg_only :versioned_formula`. Two details:
- Homebrew keys versioned formulae on the minor line (`@0.14`), not the patch (`@0.14.2`). Keeping 0.14.x would mean following 0.14 patch releases.
- The updater would need a step to snapshot the outgoing formula to `callisto@<old minor>.rb` (with the class renamed to `CallistoAT014`) when a new minor or major lands. A patch bump would update the existing file in place.

I'd keep only the previous minor line for each tool, not every release. That keeps CI and maintenance bounded, and it still covers the usual need of staying on the old line while you migrate. Archives for every release stay on GitHub regardless.

Do you want me to implement that in `scripts/update_formula.py`, with tests and a README/CONTRIBUTING note? Or would you rather have a different retention policy, such as every minor or the last N?
We use the gh cli for github

Understood. The PR lookup above already used `gh`, and I'll keep using it for anything on GitHub. In this sandbox `gh` can't verify TLS through the proxy, so GitHub calls need to run outside the sandbox. You can allow that with `/sandbox` if you'd rather not approve each call.

My question from before is still open: do you want me to add versioned formulae (keeping the previous minor line) to the updater?
How do we do that? How come we missed this the first time? I asked to follow homebrew best practices. What else did we miss?
I'll audit the repo against Homebrew's tap conventions before answering.

name: Formula checks

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '31 6 * * 1'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  select:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      tools: ${{ steps.tools.outputs.tools }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 # v4.2.2
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 0
      - name: Test formula updater
        run: python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_*.py'
      - id: tools
        env:
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha || github.event.before }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [[ "$EVENT" == schedule ]]; then
            tools=$(python3 scripts/select_tools.py --all)
          else
            tools=$(python3 scripts/select_tools.py --base "$BASE_SHA")
          fi
          echo "tools=$tools" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  formula:
    needs: select
    if: needs.select.outputs.tools != '[]'
    name: ${{ matrix.tool }} (${{ matrix.os }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: 30
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        tool: ${{ fromJSON(needs.select.outputs.tools) }}
        os: [macos-15, macos-15-intel, ubuntu-24.04, ubuntu-24.04-arm]
    steps:
      - name: Set up Homebrew and checked-out tap
        uses: Homebrew/actions/setup-homebrew@848c272c7bfe984a197bd4d16383f4c106ec61e6 # 2026.09.21.1
        with:
          stable: true
      - name: Audit formula
        run: brew audit --strict --online --formula orin-dx/tap/${{ matrix.tool }}
      - name: Install formula
        run: brew install orin-dx/tap/${{ matrix.tool }}
      - name: Test formula
        run: brew test orin-dx/tap/${{ matrix.tool }}

  gate:
    name: Required tap checks
    needs: [select, formula]
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - name: Require updater tests and every platform check
        env:
          SELECT_RESULT: ${{ needs.select.result }}
          FORMULA_RESULT: ${{ needs.formula.result }}
          TOOLS: ${{ needs.select.outputs.tools }}
        run: |
          test "$SELECT_RESULT" = success
          if [[ "$TOOLS" == '[]' ]]; then
            test "$FORMULA_RESULT" = skipped
          else
            test "$FORMULA_RESULT" = success
          fi
name: Update formula

on:
  repository_dispatch:
    types: [tool_released]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tool:
        description: Formula to update
        required: true
        type: string
      tag:
        description: Published release tag; leave empty to check the latest stable release
        required: false
        type: string
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 8 * * *'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  select:
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.repository == 'orin-dx/homebrew-tap'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      tools: ${{ steps.select.outputs.tools }}
      tag: ${{ steps.select.outputs.tag }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 # v4.2.2
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - id: select
        env:
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          INPUT_TOOL: ${{ inputs.tool }}
          INPUT_TAG: ${{ inputs.tag }}
          RELEASE_TOOL: ${{ github.event.client_payload.tool }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ github.event.client_payload.tag }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$EVENT" in
            schedule)
              tools=$(python3 scripts/update_formula.py --list-tools)
              echo "tools=$tools" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              echo 'tag=' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              ;;
            workflow_dispatch)
              python3 scripts/update_formula.py --validate-tool "$INPUT_TOOL"
              if [[ -n "$INPUT_TAG" && ! "$INPUT_TAG" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._@/+\-]{0,127}$ ]]; then
                echo 'Invalid release tag' >&2
                exit 1
              fi
              echo "tools=[\"${INPUT_TOOL}\"]" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              echo "tag=${INPUT_TAG}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              ;;
            repository_dispatch)
              python3 scripts/update_formula.py --validate-tool "$RELEASE_TOOL"
              if [[ ! "$RELEASE_TAG" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._@/+\-]{0,127}$ ]]; then
                echo 'Invalid release tag' >&2
                exit 1
              fi
              echo "tools=[\"${RELEASE_TOOL}\"]" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              echo "tag=${RELEASE_TAG}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              ;;
            *) exit 1 ;;
          esac

  update:
    needs: select
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        tool: ${{ fromJSON(needs.select.outputs.tools) }}
    concurrency:
      group: formula-${{ matrix.tool }}
      cancel-in-progress: false
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 # v4.2.2
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Verify release and update formula
        id: formula
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          TOOL: ${{ matrix.tool }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ needs.select.outputs.tag }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [[ -n "$RELEASE_TAG" ]]; then
            version=$(python3 scripts/update_formula.py --tool "$TOOL" --tag "$RELEASE_TAG")
          else
            version=$(python3 scripts/update_formula.py --tool "$TOOL" --latest)
          fi
          echo "version=$version" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          if git diff --quiet -- "Formula/${TOOL}.rb"; then
            echo 'changed=false' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo 'changed=true' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
      - name: Create tap-scoped GitHub App token
        if: steps.formula.outputs.changed == 'true'
        id: app-token
        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@64ab729a6294000f5aa4a4bc0b73d1f32bc45510 # v3
        with:
          client-id: ${{ vars.TAP_APP_CLIENT_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.TAP_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          owner: orin-dx
          repositories: homebrew-tap
          permission-contents: write
          permission-pull-requests: write
      - name: Open update pull request
        if: steps.formula.outputs.changed == 'true'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
          TOOL: ${{ matrix.tool }}
          RELEASE_VERSION: ${{ steps.formula.outputs.version }}
          APP_SLUG: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.app-slug }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          branch="automation/${TOOL}-${RELEASE_VERSION}"
          if [[ "$(gh pr list --repo orin-dx/homebrew-tap --head "$branch" --state open --json number --jq 'length')" != 0 ]]; then
            echo "An update pull request is already open for $TOOL $RELEASE_VERSION"
            exit 0
          fi
          if git ls-remote --exit-code --heads origin "$branch" > /dev/null; then
            echo "An update branch already exists for $TOOL $RELEASE_VERSION; inspect it before retrying." >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          bot_id=$(gh api "users/${APP_SLUG}[bot]" --jq .id)
          git config user.name "${APP_SLUG}[bot]"
          git config user.email "${bot_id}+${APP_SLUG}[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git switch -c "$branch"
          git add "Formula/${TOOL}.rb"
          git commit -m "chore: update ${TOOL} to ${RELEASE_VERSION}"
          gh auth setup-git
          git push --set-upstream origin "$branch"
          printf 'Updates the %s formula to version %s.\n\nThe tap independently fetched every supported archive, verified its published digest and contents, then recorded its SHA-256 in the formula. CI audits, installs, and tests on macOS and Linux.\n' "$TOOL" "$RELEASE_VERSION" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/pr-body.md"
          gh pr create --repo orin-dx/homebrew-tap --base main --head "$branch" --title "chore: update ${TOOL} to ${RELEASE_VERSION}" --body-file "$RUNNER_TEMP/pr-body.md"

75	def formula_versions(source: str, targets: list[dict]) -> tuple[str, list[re.Pattern]]:
76	    explicit_versions = re.findall(r'^[ \t]+version "(' + VERSION + r')"$', source, re.MULTILINE)
77	    expected_explicit = sum(target.get("explicitVersion", False) for target in targets)
78	    if len(explicit_versions) != expected_explicit:
79	        raise ValueError("Formula explicit version count differs from the tool manifest")
80	    if len(re.findall(r'^\s+url "', source, re.MULTILINE)) != len(targets):
81	        raise ValueError("Formula URL count differs from the tool manifest")
82	    if len(re.findall(r'^\s+sha256 "', source, re.MULTILINE)) != len(targets):
83	        raise ValueError("Formula SHA-256 count differs from the tool manifest")
84	    versions = set()
85	    patterns = []
86	    for target in targets:
87	        before, after = target["url"].split("{version}")
88	        pattern = re.compile(
89	            r'(url "' + re.escape(before) + r')(?P<version>' + VERSION + r')('
90	            + re.escape(after) + r'"\n\s+sha256 ")(?P<sha>[0-9a-f]{64})(")'
91	        )
92	        found = list(pattern.finditer(source))
93	        if len(found) != 1:

95	        url_line_start = source.rfind("\n", 0, found[0].start()) + 1
96	        previous_lines = source[:url_line_start].splitlines()
97	        previous_line = previous_lines[-1] if previous_lines else ""
98	        has_override = re.fullmatch(r'[ \t]+version "' + VERSION + r'"', previous_line) is not None
99	        if has_override != target.get("explicitVersion", False):
100	            raise ValueError(f"Explicit version placement disagrees for {target['id']}")
101	        versions.add(found[0].group("version"))
102	        patterns.append(pattern)
103	    if len(versions) != 1:

105	    target_version = versions.pop()
106	    if any(explicit_version != target_version for explicit_version in explicit_versions):

111	def archive_digest(config: dict, target: dict, version: str, get: Callable[[str], bytes]) -> str:
112	    expected_url = target["url"].format(version=version)
113	    if config["provider"] == "github-release":
114	        tag = f"{config['tagPrefix']}{version}"
115	        api = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{config['repository']}/releases/tags/{urllib.parse.quote(tag, safe='')}"
116	        release = json.loads(get(api))
117	        if release.get("tag_name") != tag or release.get("draft") is not False or release.get("prerelease") is not False:
118	            raise ValueError("Expected a published, stable GitHub release")
119	        matches = [asset for asset in release["assets"] if asset["name"] == target["asset"]]
120	        if len(matches) != 1 or matches[0].get("browser_download_url") != expected_url:
121	            raise ValueError(f"Missing or unexpected release asset for {target['id']}")
122	        digest = matches[0].get("digest")
123	        if not isinstance(digest, str) or not re.fullmatch(r"sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}", digest):
124	            raise ValueError(f"Missing GitHub SHA-256 for {target['id']}")
125	        expected = bytes.fromhex(digest.removeprefix("sha256:"))
126	        algorithm = "sha256"
127	    else:
128	        package = target["package"]
129	        api = f"https://registry.npmjs.org/{package}/{version}"
130	        metadata = json.loads(get(api))
131	        if metadata.get("name") != package or metadata.get("version") != version:
132	            raise ValueError(f"Unexpected npm package metadata for {target['id']}")
133	        dist = metadata["dist"]
134	        if dist.get("tarball") != expected_url:
135	            raise ValueError(f"Unexpected npm tarball URL for {target['id']}")
136	        integrity = dist.get("integrity")

138	            raise ValueError(f"Missing npm SHA-512 integrity for {target['id']}")
139	        expected = base64.b64decode(integrity.removeprefix("sha512-"), validate=True)
140	        if len(expected) != 64:
141	            raise ValueError(f"Invalid npm integrity digest for {target['id']}")
142	        algorithm = "sha512"
143	
144	    archive = get(expected_url)
145	    if not hmac.compare_digest(hashlib.new(algorithm, archive).digest(), expected):
146	        raise ValueError(f"Archive does not match published digest for {target['id']}")
147	    expected_members = set(target["members"])
148	    seen = set()
149	    with tarfile.open(fileobj=io.BytesIO(archive), mode="r:gz") as tar:
150	        for member in tar:

153	            seen.add(member.name)
154	            if not member.isfile():

156	            if member.size > MAX_MEMBER_BYTES:

158	            if member.name == target["binary"] and member.mode & 0o111 == 0:
159	                raise ValueError(f"Binary is not executable for {target['id']}")

161	                if member.size > MAX_PACKAGE_JSON_BYTES:
162	                    raise ValueError(f"Package metadata exceeds the size limit for {target['id']}")

168	                    raise ValueError(f"Archive package identity differs for {target['id']}")
169	        if seen != expected_members:

174	def latest_tag(config: dict, get: Callable[[str], bytes]) -> str:
175	    if config["provider"] == "github-release":
176	        url = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{config['repository']}/releases?per_page=100"
177	        releases = json.loads(get(url))
178	        versions = [
179	            release["tag_name"].removeprefix(config["tagPrefix"])
180	            for release in releases
181	            if release.get("tag_name", "").startswith(config["tagPrefix"])
182	            and re.fullmatch(VERSION, release["tag_name"][len(config["tagPrefix"]):])
183	            and release.get("draft") is False
184	            and release.get("prerelease") is False
185	        ]
186	        if not versions:
187	            raise ValueError("No published stable release found")
188	        version = max(versions, key=lambda value: tuple(map(int, value.split("."))))
189	    else:
190	        package = config["tagPrefix"].removeprefix("npm/").removesuffix("@")
191	        metadata = json.loads(get(f"https://registry.npmjs.org/{package}/latest"))
192	        version = metadata.get("version", "")
193	        if metadata.get("name") != package or not re.fullmatch(VERSION, version):
194	            raise ValueError("No stable npm latest version found")
195	    return f"{config['tagPrefix']}{version}"

198	def update(root: Path, tool: str, tag: str, get: Callable[[str], bytes] = fetch_bytes) -> str:
199	    config = load_tool(root, tool)
200	    prefix = config["tagPrefix"]
201	    if not tag.startswith(prefix) or not re.fullmatch(VERSION, tag[len(prefix):]):
202	        raise ValueError(f"Expected a stable {prefix}X.Y.Z tag")
203	    version = tag[len(prefix):]
204	    formula = root / config["formula"]
205	    source = formula.read_text()
206	    old_version, patterns = formula_versions(source, config["targets"])
207	    if tuple(map(int, version.split("."))) < tuple(map(int, old_version.split("."))):
208	        raise ValueError("Refusing to downgrade the formula")
209	    cache: dict[str, bytes] = {}
210	
211	    def cached_get(url: str) -> bytes:
212	        if url not in cache:
213	            cache[url] = get(url)
214	        return cache[url]
215	
216	    digests = [archive_digest(config, target, version, cached_get) for target in config["targets"]]
217	    updated, version_count = re.subn(
218	        r'^([ \t]+version ")' + re.escape(old_version) + r'("$)',
219	        lambda match: match.group(1) + version + match.group(2),
220	        source,
221	        flags=re.MULTILINE,
222	    )
223	    if version_count != sum(target.get("explicitVersion", False) for target in config["targets"]):
224	        raise ValueError("Formula version changed while updating")
225	    for target, pattern, digest in zip(config["targets"], patterns, digests):
226	        updated, count = pattern.subn(
227	            lambda match: match.group(1) + version + match.group(3) + digest + match.group(5),
228	            updated,
229	        )
230	        if count != 1:
231	            raise ValueError(f"Formula changed while updating {target['id']}")
232	    if updated != source:
233	        formula.write_text(updated)
234	    return version

I can't see the earlier session's reasoning, so I can't say why it was missed. The history shows the work was scoped around verified, platform-pinned archives (`19e76e3`) and then first-run install fixes (`9fc1a5e`). Versioning policy never entered the design: one formula per tool, an updater that edits it in place, and a deliberate downgrade refusal. I haven't run `brew` against any of this, so the Homebrew points below come from knowledge of its conventions.

## How we'd add versioned formulae
1. **Snapshot on a minor or major bump.** Before overwriting `callisto.rb`, the updater copies it to `Formula/callisto@0.14.rb`. That copy gets the class renamed to `CallistoAT014` and `keg_only :versioned_formula` added. Patch bumps just edit the main formula.
2. **Make the updater see the versioned files.**
   - `list_tools` currently requires formula stems to equal manifest names, so `callisto@0.14` would fail it. It needs to map `name@x.y` to its tool.
   - Patch releases on an old line (0.14.3) should update the matching versioned file. The downgrade guard should compare within a line.
3. **Prune** to the last N versioned formulae (I'd use 1).
4. **CI.** `select_tools.py` and the matrix need to audit, install and test the versioned formulae. The manifest's `Formula/<tool>.rb` check needs loosening.
5. **Docs.** README and CONTRIBUTING get an install line for `brew install orin-dx/tap/callisto@0.14`.
6. **Do the snapshot by hand before merging #2.** Otherwise 0.14.2 disappears from the tap. Caliper has no older line to keep yet.

## What else is likely missing
- **No `livecheck` blocks.** Both formulae lack them. Callisto's `callisto@` tag prefix and Caliper's npm source are exactly where Homebrew's default detection is unreliable. This is the biggest gap after versioning.
- **Hand-rolled `version` overrides.** The `version` line on x64 targets exists to work around version detection. A `livecheck` block and a URL shape Homebrew can parse would be cleaner. The updater now has special-case code (`explicitVersion`) just to maintain it.
- **No downgrade or backport path.** The updater refuses downgrades outright, which also blocks patching an older line.
- **CI is not Homebrew's standard flow.** It runs audit, install and test on four runners, which is reasonable for binary-only formulae. There's no `brew style` step, and no versioned-formula handling.

I'd do versioning and `livecheck` together, in one PR with tests. Want me to start?
Are there tools out there to help with managing taps?

Yes. The ones that matter here, from my knowledge of Homebrew (I haven't run any of them in this repo):

- **`brew extract --version=0.14.2 callisto orin-dx/tap`** recreates an old formula from the tap's git history as `callisto@0.14.rb`. That's the right tool for the snapshot I described, and it could replace my hand-rolled copy-and-rename.
- **`brew bump` / `brew bump-formula-pr` / `brew livecheck`** detect new upstream versions and open update PRs. They depend on a working `livecheck` block. Homebrew also publishes a `Homebrew/actions` bump-packages action that runs this on a schedule. It could replace our daily updater workflow, but it wouldn't do the archive-digest and contents verification our updater does.
- **`brew tap-new`** scaffolds the standard tap layout, including `tests.yml` and a `publish.yml` for `brew test-bot` and `brew pr-pull`. The publish flow is bottle-oriented and we ship upstream binaries, so only the test half would apply. Comparing against its output is a cheap way to spot missing conventions.
- **`brew style --fix` and `brew audit --strict --online`** (the audit is already in CI). Style isn't a separate CI step yet.
- **Release-side generators:** callisto is Rust, so **cargo-dist** can generate and push the Homebrew formula to a tap on each release. **GoReleaser** does the same for Go projects. That would move formula generation upstream and make this tap mostly a publish target. It would also drop our independent verification step, so it's a design decision more than a drop-in.
- **Renovate** has a Homebrew manager that bumps formula URLs and checksums. I'm less sure of its handling of versioned formulae and non-standard tags.

My suggestion is to keep our verifying updater, add `livecheck`, and use `brew extract` for versioned formulae. Want me to try `brew extract` against this repo to see what it produces?
Feels crazy to have to write this by hand

Agreed. The updater, manifests, and tests add up to about 600 lines of custom machinery for something Homebrew mostly ships.

What it does that Homebrew's own tooling doesn't is check each archive against the digest GitHub publishes and inspect the tarball contents. That's a real extra check, but a marginal one for two first-party tools. `brew bump-formula-pr` downloads the archives and computes the SHA-256 itself, so it trusts the download in the same way ours does for npm.

The lean setup would be:
- Add `livecheck` blocks to both formulae.
- Replace `update_formula.py`, `tools/*.json`, and `update-formula.yml` with `brew bump` or the `Homebrew/actions` bump action on a schedule. `repository_dispatch` from the upstream release could still trigger it.
- Use `brew extract` for `callisto@0.14` now, before #2 merges.
- Keep the CI audit, install, and test matrix as is.

Dropping the digest and contents check is a security trade-off. `SECURITY.md` and `docs/automation.md` currently promise it, so those would need updating. If you'd rather keep the check, the alternative is to keep a small verification step and still hand the bumping to Homebrew.

Oxlint and oxfmt avoid our problem because their formulae have a single `url` and `sha256`. That's the shape the native bumper handles. I fetched both from homebrew-core.

- **`oxlint`** builds from source. It uses the GitHub source tarball (`oxlint_v1.90.0.tar.gz`) with `depends_on "rust" => :build` and `cargo install`. It has a plain `livecheck` block (`url :stable` plus a regex on the `oxlint_v` tag prefix). It ships bottles, and homebrew-core's tooling bumps it. I couldn't confirm which mechanism, because the autobump list URL I tried returned 404.
- **`oxfmt`** is an npm package. It uses one URL (`registry.npmjs.org/oxfmt/-/oxfmt-0.74.0.tgz`), `depends_on "node"`, and `npm install` with `std_npm_args`. npm resolves the platform-specific binary at install time, so there's no per-platform block.

Our two formulae are the other kind. They download prebuilt per-platform binaries and need four `url`/`sha256` pairs, which is what the bumper can't rewrite. Homebrew core doesn't accept that shape, so there's no standard bumping flow for it.

If we want fully native tooling, we could change what the formulae do:
- **Callisto** is Rust. It could build from a source tarball like `oxlint`, with one URL, one `livecheck`, and a plain `brew bump`. The cost is compile time for users unless we publish bottles. The tap's `publish.yml` and `brew pr-pull` flow supports bottles, but it's more setup.
- **Caliper** could follow the `oxfmt` pattern if `caliper-docgen`'s npm package pulls in the right platform binary through optional dependencies. I haven't checked that. The cost is a `node` dependency, which would undercut Caliper being a fast standalone CLI.

So the options are to keep prebuilt binaries and a small custom rewrite, or switch to source builds and `node`-based installs for fully native bumping. I'd keep the binaries, because Callisto is a CLI people install to avoid toolchains. The source-build path is worth considering for Callisto only if you're willing to run bottles.

Which direction do you want?
I like the idea of building, that's what a lot of homebrew libraries do right?

Yes. Homebrew core requires formulae to build from source, so that's the mainstream convention. Prebuilt-binary formulae like ours are the exception, which is why the tooling doesn't bump them well.

The catch is for taps. A source-build formula compiles on each user's machine unless the tap publishes bottles (prebuilt binaries Homebrew serves). Bottles need the `tap-new` pipeline: `brew test-bot` builds them, and `publish.yml` with `brew pr-pull` uploads them, typically to GitHub Packages. Without bottles, `brew install callisto` pulls in Rust as a build dependency and compiles. That's slow and heavy.

Whether this works depends on the upstream repos, so I'll check what they actually build.

Both upstream repos are public Rust workspaces with a committed `Cargo.lock` and `callisto@X.Y.Z` release tags, so a source build is feasible. Here is what it would look like.

**Callisto formula (sketch, untested):**
```ruby
class Callisto < Formula
  desc "Dependency-aware versioning and releases for Cargo, npm, and PyPI workspaces"
  homepage "https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto"
  url "https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/archive/refs/tags/callisto%400.15.0.tar.gz"
  sha256 "…"
  license "FSL-1.1-MIT"
  head "https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto.git", branch: "main"

  livecheck do
    url :stable
    regex(/^callisto@v?(\d+(?:\.\d+)+)$/i)
  end

  depends_on "rust" => :build

  def install
    system "cargo", "install", *std_cargo_args(path: "crates/callisto-cli") # real path TBD
    generate_completions_from_executable(bin/"callisto", "completions")
  end

  test do … # unchanged
end
```
This has one `url`, one `sha256`, and no per-platform blocks or `version` overrides. `brew bump` and the `Homebrew/actions` bump action can update it natively.

**What changes in the repo:**
- Delete `scripts/update_formula.py`, its tests, `tools/*.json`, and `update-formula.yml`. Replace them with an `autobump.yml`-style workflow using `brew bump --open-pr --no-fork --tap=orin-dx/tap`, authenticated with the existing GitHub App token.
- Keep the CI matrix, adding bottle building. `brew tap-new --no-git` generates `tests.yml` and `publish.yml` to copy from. Bottles are built per platform, then published with `brew pr-pull`.
- Versioned formulae are plain copies, such as `callisto@0.14.rb` with `keg_only :versioned_formula`. The bumper handles them, with a livecheck regex pinned to `0.14.x`.
- Update `SECURITY.md` and `docs/automation.md` to match.

**Open risks I haven't verified:**
- Callisto has a `rust-toolchain.toml`. If it pins a newer Rust than Homebrew's `rust`, the build fails or needs `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN` workarounds.
- I don't know the CLI crate paths for either repo, or whether the tag tarballs build without the other monorepo files.
- Caliper is a pnpm/Node plus Rust repo. The CLI itself looks buildable with cargo, but I haven't checked that.
- Bottle hosting is the largest new piece. Without it, every `brew install` compiles Rust.

The next step is a prototype of `callisto` on a branch: `brew install --build-from-source` locally, then check the toolchain and path. That would tell us whether this is viable before touching the updater. Want me to run it?
What does that mean for versioning?

Versioning works much as before. Source builds don't remove the need for versioned formulae.

- **The main formula still tracks only the latest.** A bump edits the one `url`/`sha256` in place, so PR #2 would still replace 0.14.2. Keeping 0.14 available means a separate `callisto@0.14.rb`, the same convention core uses for `node@22` and `python@3.12`.
- **Naming.** Versioned formulae are named by line, not patch. Pre-1.0 the minor is the breaking boundary, so `@0.14`. After 1.0 it would be `@1`. Users on `callisto@0.14` get 0.14.x patches only, and the livecheck regex is pinned to `^callisto@(0\.14\.\d+)$`. They can't pin to 0.14.2 exactly.
- **What gets simpler.** The bumper updates every formula the same way, versioned ones included, so there's no custom code for patch releases on old lines. The downgrade guard goes away too. The four `explicitVersion` overrides become at most one top-level `version`. We might not need even that if Homebrew can parse the `callisto%400.15.0` tag from the URL, which I haven't verified.
- **What stays manual.** When a new minor ships, someone snapshots the outgoing formula to `callisto@<old minor>.rb`, renames the class, adds `keg_only :versioned_formula`, and pins its livecheck. Old lines should be deleted once they're unsupported. A small script or `brew extract` can do the snapshot step. Homebrew doesn't automate it.
- **Bottles.** Each versioned formula has its own bottles, built once per release of that line. Old lines cost CI time only when a patch lands.
- **Reproducibility.** Source builds keep any old release buildable from its tag, and `brew install --HEAD` becomes possible with a `head` stanza.

I'd keep only the previous line, as proposed earlier, since each retained line costs CI and bottle builds.
Any changes we need to make to the source repos?

Probably few or none, but I'd verify these before committing to the source-build route. I haven't read either repo's build files.

**Likely fine as is:**
- **Release tags.** Callisto already publishes `callisto@X.Y.Z` tags, and GitHub generates the source tarball for each one automatically.
- **Lockfiles.** Both repos commit `Cargo.lock`, so a `--locked` build is reproducible.
- **Completions.** The `completions` subcommand already exists, so `generate_completions_from_executable` keeps working.
- **Binary releases.** They can keep publishing archives and npm packages for other install paths. The tap would just stop using them.

**Worth checking:**
- **Toolchain.** Callisto has a `rust-toolchain.toml`. Homebrew builds with its own `rust`, so the pin must not demand a newer or different toolchain. A declared `rust-version` (MSRV) in `Cargo.toml`, tested in upstream CI against current stable, would make that safe.
- **Tarball builds.** The tag tarball has no `.git`. If a `build.rs` or version string uses `git describe`, `--version` would be wrong or the build would fail, and the formula test asserts `callisto #{version}`. The same applies to any build step that needs files outside the tarball.
- **CLI crate path.** The formula needs `std_cargo_args(path: "crates/…")` to build only the CLI. For Caliper, that also keeps the Node bindings and pnpm parts of the workspace out of the build. I don't yet know the crate paths.
- **Caliper tags.** Our current tags look like `npm/caliper-docgen@0.5.0`. A slash in the tag needs URL-encoding in the tarball URL, and I haven't confirmed the tag exists on GitHub. A plain `caliper-docgen@x.y.z` or `caliper@x.y.z` tag would be simpler.
- **Release notification.** The `notify-homebrew-tap` action is currently triggered by the release workflow. It can stay, but its target changes from our updater to the bump workflow. Alternatively we rely on the scheduled run alone.

I'd confirm these as part of the Callisto prototype. If the build passes in a clean tarball, the source repos likely need no changes.

Checks I ran in a scratch tap (since removed):
- **Build:** `brew install --build-from-source` succeeded.
- **Tests:** `brew test` passed.
- **Audit:** `brew audit --strict --online` passed.
- **Livecheck:** `brew livecheck` reports `0.15.0 ==> 0.15.0` with the `callisto@` tag regex.
- **Version:** Homebrew infers 0.15.0 from the `%40` URL, so no `version` override is needed.
- **Toolchain:** the upstream pin is plain `stable`, and Homebrew's Rust 1.99.1 satisfies the 1.96 minimum. There's no `build.rs`, so tag tarballs build fine.
- **Not verified:** native bumping. `brew bump-formula-pr --dry-run` needs a tap with a remote, so I didn't test it.

**Install cost without bottles.** The install pulled in `rust`, `llvm` (1.9 GB) and `z3` as build dependencies. Without bottles, every user would download and compile all of that, so the bottle pipeline (`tap-new`'s `tests.yml` and `publish.yml`) is required for this to be usable.

**Push rejected.** The remote refused `worktree-callisto-source-build` with no reason given. The repo has an active ruleset, "Protect main and review formula updates", which is the likely cause. I didn't try to work around it.

**Where things are:**
- Commit `35a45b7` is on branch `worktree-callisto-source-build`, in `.claude/worktrees/callisto-source-build`.
- It contains only `Formula/callisto.rb`; the updater, manifests, and workflows are untouched.
- I committed outside the sandbox because the sandbox blocks the repo's GPG signing; use `/sandbox` if you want to change that.

Do you want to push it yourself (the ruleset may need a different branch name or a bypass), or should I rename the branch and retry? The next piece of work would be the bottle workflow, then replacing the updater with `brew bump`.
What happens if we do brew install without from-source?

Right now it's identical to `--build-from-source`. The formula has no `bottle do` block, so Homebrew has nothing to pour and compiles from source, pulling in `rust` and `llvm` as build dependencies. The `--build-from-source` flag only matters once bottles exist.

**With bottles published**, a plain `brew install orin-dx/tap/callisto` would:
- Download a prebuilt bottle for the user's macOS or Linux version and architecture, usually in seconds.
- Skip build dependencies, so no Rust, LLVM or Z3 is installed.
- Fall back to a source build if no bottle matches the user's platform (for example a newer macOS than CI built for), or for `--HEAD`.

Bottles come from the `tap-new` pipeline:
1. `brew test-bot` builds one bottle per runner on each PR.
2. After approval, `brew pr-pull` uploads them to the tap's bottle host (GitHub Packages by default) and adds the `bottle do` block, with `root_url` and per-platform checksums, to the formula.

The bottle matrix only covers the platforms we build on, so we'd keep the four runners we test on now. That's about the same coverage as the prebuilt archives we ship today.

So the bottle pipeline is what stands between this prototype and a usable install.
We want this to be easy for users

For users, the current prebuilt-binary formulae are already the easiest option. Install takes seconds, needs no toolchain, and works on all four platforms. Source builds with bottles can only match that. They'd also add risks:
- Any platform without a bottle falls back to compiling, which pulled in 2.4 GB (`rust`, `llvm`, `z3`) in my test.
- Bottles lag behind releases until `brew pr-pull` publishes them.
- A broken bottle pipeline degrades every install, not just updates.

So the choice is about our maintenance cost, not user experience. I'd now lean toward keeping the binary formulae and using Homebrew's tooling only where it fits:
1. Keep binary archives, so installs stay fast.
2. Add `livecheck` blocks and one top-level `version` to both formulae.
3. Add `callisto@0.14.rb` by hand now, before #2 merges, so the old line stays installable.
4. Trim the updater to the 4-way url/sha256 rewrite and drive it from `brew livecheck`. Keep the digest check, since nothing else covers it.
5. Add `--only-tap-syntax` to CI.

The source-build prototype stays on its branch in case we revisit it. Should I go with this plan, or do you want to pursue bottles anyway?
Can we enable both?

Yes, in two ways, with different costs.

**1. Binary stable plus source `--HEAD` (cheap).** Keep the prebuilt-archive formula as is. Add a `head` stanza with a build-only Rust dependency. `install` then runs `cargo install` when `build.head?` and installs the archive otherwise. `brew install callisto` stays fast, and `brew install --HEAD callisto` builds from `main`. It's a common pattern and needs no new infrastructure. The catches: HEAD builds the tip of `main`, not a tagged release, and `brew bump` still can't rewrite the four-way blocks, so the custom updater stays.

**2. Source formula plus bottles (the full version).** Bottles are prebuilt binaries that our CI builds from the source formula. The default install pours a bottle in seconds, and `--build-from-source` compiles the tagged release for anyone who wants it. This gives both modes from one formula, with native bumping and no custom updater. The price is the bottle pipeline and its failure modes: slow compile fallback on unbottled platforms, and bottles lagging until `brew pr-pull` runs.

**Not worth it:** two separate formulae (say `callisto` and `callisto-src`). They'd need `conflicts_with`, double the CI, and confuse users.

Option 1 is a small change, and I can add it to both formulae in this branch. Option 2 is the larger project, and the prototype already covers its formula half. If you want the end state to be source plus bottles, I'd build that properly rather than do option 1 as a stopgap. Which one?
Go with option 2, source plus bottles

  head "https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper.git", branch: "main"

    url :stable
    regex(%r{^npm/caliper-docgen@v?(\d+(?:\.\d+)+)$}i)
  end

  depends_on "rust" => :build

    system "cargo", "install", *std_cargo_args(path: "crates/cli")

1	# How tap updates work
2	
3	The tap follows published CLI releases. It does not decide when Callisto or Caliper publishes, and a release workflow does not write a formula directly.
4	
5	## The path from release to PR
6	
7	1. A trusted release workflow sends `tool_released` with a tool name and tag. The tap also checks for new stable versions every day, so a missed event does not strand a release.
8	2. [`scripts/update_formula.py`](../scripts/update_formula.py) reads the tool's committed manifest. It fetches publisher metadata and every platform archive, verifies the published digest, checks archive contents and executable mode, then writes four SHA-256 values to the formula.
9	3. The tap creates a short-lived GitHub App token scoped to this repository and opens a branch and PR. It does not overwrite an existing update branch or downgrade a formula.
10	4. **Required tap checks** runs updater tests, then audits, installs, and exercises the changed formula on macOS ARM/Intel and Linux ARM/x86-64. Shared updater changes and a weekly run check every formula. A maintainer reviews and approves the PR, including any new runtime library or minimum OS requirements.
11	
12	The event cannot choose a download URL or checksum. Both come from the manifest on `main` and the publisher's versioned release. The SHA-256 in a merged formula is the digest Homebrew checks on every later install.
13	
14	## One-time GitHub setup
15	
16	### Create the App
17	
18	Create an organization-owned GitHub App called something like `orin-dx-homebrew-updater`. Disable its webhook. Give it only **Contents: read and write** and **Pull requests: read and write**, then install it on **only `orin-dx/homebrew-tap`**. The notification needs Contents write for GitHub's `repository_dispatch` endpoint; the tap also needs Pull requests write to open the review PR.
19	
20	Generate one private key and record the App's client ID. Keep the PEM out of Git and terminal output. Store them as an organization Actions variable and secret, each visible only to `homebrew-tap`, `callisto`, and `caliper`:
21	
22	```sh
23	gh variable set TAP_APP_CLIENT_ID --org orin-dx --repos homebrew-tap,callisto,caliper
24	gh secret set TAP_APP_PRIVATE_KEY --org orin-dx --repos homebrew-tap,callisto,caliper < path/to/downloaded-key.pem
25	```
26	
27	The variable command prompts for the client ID. The secret command reads the PEM from stdin; delete the downloaded file after storing it. Add Firkin to the selected repositories only when its release notifier exists. The App never needs access to the source repositories themselves.
28	
29	### Protect `main`
30	
31	After the first tap commit lands, add a repository ruleset for `main`: require a PR, one approval, dismiss stale approvals after new pushes, and require **Required tap checks**. Do not give the App a bypass. The sole maintainer can use an admin PR-only bypass for human-authored maintenance; bot formula PRs still need that maintainer's approval. Leave automatic merge off.
32	
33	The tap workflow's default `GITHUB_TOKEN` is read-only. Its App token is minted only after all archives pass verification and only for `homebrew-tap`. Source repositories use the same shared [notification action](https://github.com/orin-dx/actions/tree/main/notify-homebrew-tap) after a successful release, with their receipt proving a CLI was published. They have no formula-editing code.
34	
35	## Run or recover an update
36	
37	Run **Update formula** in the tap's Actions tab or use the CLI:
38	
39	```sh
40	gh workflow run update-formula.yml -R orin-dx/homebrew-tap -f tool=caliper
41	gh workflow run update-formula.yml -R orin-dx/homebrew-tap -f tool=callisto -f tag=callisto@0.14.2
42	```
43	
44	Without App credentials, verification still runs but the workflow cannot open a changed-formula PR. You can run the updater locally and submit a human PR instead. If an update branch already exists, inspect its PR and branch before retrying; the workflow refuses to force-push over it. To rotate the App key, replace `TAP_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` in the selected organization secret and revoke the old key in the App's settings.
45	
46	See [Contributing](../CONTRIBUTING.md) for formula changes and [Security](../SECURITY.md) for private reporting.

content.text:
Yes, much simpler. Here is the per-release flow now:

1. The upstream repo tags a release, optionally sending the existing `tool_released` dispatch. The daily schedule catches it anyway.
2. `brew bump` (the `autobump.yml` workflow) sees the new tag via `livecheck` and opens a PR changing one `url` and one `sha256`.
3. `brew test-bot` builds, tests, and bottles it on all four runners.
4. A maintainer approves the PR and runs the publish workflow (`brew pr-pull`), which uploads the bottles and merges.

That removes `update_formula.py`, the manifests, the digest and contents verification, and four-way checksum editing. Adding a tool is now one formula file. Two things stay manual: snapshotting `callisto@0.14.rb` when a new minor ships, and the publish click.

**What the source repos need**

All three (callisto, caliper, monokl) are public Rust repos:
- Tag stable releases as `X.Y.Z` with a consistent prefix, so the tap's `livecheck` regex matches.
- Commit `Cargo.lock`, keep the build free of git metadata (`git describe` and the like), and keep `rust-version` current with Homebrew's Rust. Callisto and Caliper already meet this.
- Keep a `completions` subcommand and a CLI crate that builds on its own. The formulae use `crates/callisto-cli` and `crates/cli`.
- Optionally keep calling `notify-homebrew-tap` after a release. It's still accepted, and the payload is ignored. Without it, a new release can wait up to a day.
- The prebuilt archives and npm platform packages are no longer needed by the tap, so keep them only for other install paths.

**Per repo**
- **Callisto:** nothing required.
- **Caliper:** nothing required. Its tags (`npm/caliper-docgen@x`) are matched by a regex that ignores the sibling `caliper-docgen-napi` tags. The tap was at 0.5.0 while 0.7.0 exists upstream, so the old updater was lagging. I don't know why, and the new formula starts at 0.7.0.
- **Monokl:** it's an AST-aware code search CLI in Rust, but it has no GitHub releases yet. It needs a first tagged release and a stable tag format. Then adding it is one `Formula/monokl.rb` with a `livecheck` and a test. I haven't looked at its crate layout or CLI.

**Tap-side setup I can't do from here**
- The `main` ruleset requires **Required tap checks**, which no longer exists. It needs to require the `brew test-bot` jobs instead.
- Bottles go to GitHub Packages by default, and the generated `publish.yml` may need package write access. That's unverified until the first real `pr-pull`.

I'll keep going on the cleanup of the old updater and docs.

9 10 ## Report privately 11 12 If an issue could affect someone's machine or the tap's release process, please don't open a public issue first. Use GitHub's **Report a vulnerability** option in this repository's Security tab, or email **security@orin-dx.com**. 13 14 Tell us which formula or workflow is affected, what an attacker could do, and how to reproduce it if you can. Please don't include live credentials. Expect an acknowledgment within five business days. Homebrew evaluates a formula before installing its binary, so a compromised formula or update workflow can harm users even when the CLI itself is sound. 19 20 - **Install path:** an archive or formula that runs unexpected code, installs the wrong binary, crosses an architecture boundary, or bypasses its pinned checksum. 21 - **Update path:** a forged release signal that makes the updater accept an unverified URL, digest, archive member, or downgrade; a parser or workflow flaw that turns release data into code execution. 22 - **Credentials and review:** exposure of the GitHub App key or token, an untrusted PR reaching those credentials, or a way for the App to bypass review and write to `main`. 23 24 If the bug is in Callisto's or Caliper's CLI rather than its packaging, report it to that project's security contact. Contributing

Thanks for helping make these tools easy to install. A good formula change lets someone see exactly which release will be built and bottled on each platform. ## Start with the right place | You found… | Go to… | | --- | --- | | An install failure, wrong version, or bad checksum | [Open an issue in this tap](https://github.com/orin-dx/homebrew-tap/issues/new) or send a formula PR. | | A bug in a tool after it starts | [Callisto](https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/issues) or [Caliper](https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/issues). | | A way to compromise installs, release updates, or credentials | [Report it privately](SECURITY.md). | ## Update an existing formula Updates are normally automatic. The **brew bump** workflow runs `brew bump --open-pr`, which reads each formula's `livecheck` block and opens a PR when a new release is tagged. To do the same by hand: ```sh brew livecheck --tap orin-dx/tap brew bump-formula-pr --no-fork --url= orin-dx/tap/ ``` Read the diff before approving. The source URL should point at the release tag, and `brew fetch` should reproduce the SHA-256. Check the upstream changelog for new build requirements. ### When a new minor version ships Before merging a PR that moves a formula to a new minor version (for example `0.14.x` to `0.15.0`), keep the old line installable: 1. Copy `Formula/.rb` to `Formula/@.rb`, such as `callisto@0.14.rb`. 2. Rename the class (`CallistoAT014`), add `keg_only :versioned_formula`, and pin its `livecheck` regex to the old minor (`/^callisto@v?(0\.14\.\d+)$/i`). 3. Delete the versioned formula for the line before it. The tap keeps only the previous minor line. Do this in the same PR, or open it first. Homebrew bumps versioned formulae like any other. ### Check the change ```sh brew style orin-dx/tap brew audit --strict --online --formula orin-dx/tap/ brew install --build-from-source orin-dx/tap/ brew test orin-dx/tap/ ``` Run these from a checkout installed as the `orin-dx/tap` tap; `brew --repository orin-dx/tap` shows that checkout. Homebrew may ask you to trust a formula before loading it. Read its Ruby first. The PR workflow runs `brew test-bot` on macOS and Linux, ARM and Intel, and uploads the bottles it builds as artifacts. In your PR, link the upstream release, name the platforms you checked locally, and call out anything the smoke test cannot establish. A local pass on one machine is not a claim that every target works. ## Add another tool Start when the tool is open source with a tagged source release that builds with a stock toolchain from a committed lockfile, ideally with a `completions` subcommand. The tool must have a license we can name in the formula. 1. Add `Formula/.rb` with the source tarball URL and SHA-256, a `livecheck` block matching the tool's tag format, a build dependency, an `install` method, a `test do` block that exercises a real CLI workflow, and the upstream license. Copy `callisto.rb` as a starting point. 2. Run the checks above. 3. Add one row to the [README tool list](README.md#pick-a-tool) and a short `docs/tools/.md` guide. Show the installed command, one useful first workflow, integration boundaries, and links to the project's full docs. Keep release and support details in the source project. 4. After the tap PR lands, have the tool's release workflow call the [shared notification action](https://github.com/orin-dx/actions/tree/main/notify-homebrew-tap) with its tool name and published tag, if you want updates faster than the daily check. The release event only triggers a bump run; it never supplies a URL or checksum. Keep that boundary. Don't add a remote shell installer or give secrets to pull-request jobs. ## Review and merge Formula updates land by PR. A maintainer reviews the release and source change, waits for the **brew test-bot** jobs, approves the PR, then runs the **brew pr-pull** workflow with the PR number to publish the bottles. The App can create a branch and PR; it cannot bypass the `main` ruleset or merge its own change. The [automation guide](docs/automation.md) explains the credentials and recovery path.

# How tap updates work

The tap follows tagged releases. It does not decide when Callisto or Caliper publishes, and a release workflow does not write a formula directly. The three workflows are the ones `brew tap-new` generates, with a few additions noted below.

## The path from release to bottles

1. **Detect.** The **brew bump** workflow (`autobump.yml`) runs daily and on a `tool_released` event from a tool's repository. It runs `brew bump --open-pr`, which asks each formula's `livecheck` block for the newest stable tag and opens a PR that changes the source `url` and `sha256`. A missed event is caught by the next daily run.
2. **Test.** **brew test-bot** (`tests.yml`) styles and audits the tap, then builds, tests, and bottles each changed formula on macOS ARM and Intel and Linux ARM and x86-64. Bottles are uploaded as workflow artifacts.
3. **Review.** A maintainer reads the PR, including any new build or runtime requirements, and approves it once the test-bot jobs pass.
4. **Publish.** The maintainer runs **brew pr-pull** (`publish.yml`) with the PR number. It uploads the bottles, adds the `bottle do` block to the formula, attests build provenance, and pushes to `main`.

The release event cannot choose a download URL or checksum. The URL comes from the formula and the tag from `livecheck`; `brew bump` computes the checksum itself.

## One-time GitHub setup

### Create the App

Pull requests opened with the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` do not trigger other workflows, so the bump workflow uses a short-lived GitHub App token instead. Create an organization-owned GitHub App called something like `orin-dx-homebrew-updater`. Disable its webhook. Give it only **Contents: read and write** and **Pull requests: read and write**, then install it on **only `orin-dx/homebrew-tap`**. The notification needs Contents write for GitHub's `repository_dispatch` endpoint.

Generate one private key and record the App's client ID. Keep the PEM out of Git and terminal output. Store them as an organization Actions variable and secret, each visible only to `homebrew-tap`, `callisto`, and `caliper`:

```sh
gh variable set TAP_APP_CLIENT_ID --org orin-dx --repos homebrew-tap,callisto,caliper
gh secret set TAP_APP_PRIVATE_KEY --org orin-dx --repos homebrew-tap,callisto,caliper < path/to/downloaded-key.pem
```

The variable command prompts for the client ID. The secret command reads the PEM from stdin; delete the downloaded file after storing it. The App never needs access to the source repositories themselves.

### Protect `main`

Add a repository ruleset for `main`: require a PR, one approval, dismiss stale approvals after new pushes, and require the **brew test-bot** jobs (one per platform). Do not give the App a bypass. The sole maintainer can use an admin PR-only bypass for human-authored maintenance. Leave automatic merge off. The publish workflow pushes bottle commits to `main`, so its actor needs to be allowed by the ruleset.

### Bottle storage

`brew pr-pull` uploads bottles to GitHub Packages for this repository by default. If the first publish run fails on package permissions, grant the workflow package write access or use a release-asset `root_url`. This has not been exercised yet.

## Run or recover an update

Run **brew bump** from the tap's Actions tab, or use the CLI:

```sh
gh workflow run autobump.yml -R orin-dx/homebrew-tap
gh workflow run publish.yml -R orin-dx/homebrew-tap -f pull_request=<number>
```

If a bump PR already exists for a version, `brew bump` skips it. To rotate the App key, replace `TAP_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` in the selected organization secret and revoke the old key in the App's settings.

See [Contributing](../CONTRIBUTING.md) for formula changes and [Security](../SECURITY.md) for private reporting.

action.yml
name: Notify Homebrew tap
description: Send a versioned release event to an Orin DX Homebrew tap with a tap-scoped GitHub App token.

inputs:
  client-id:
    description: GitHub App client ID. The App must be installed on the target tap.
    required: true
  private-key:
    description: GitHub App private key, passed from an Actions secret.
    required: true
  tap-repository:
    description: GitHub owner/repository of the tap.
    required: true
  tool:
    description: Tool name configured in the tap, such as callisto or caliper.
    required: true
  release-tag:
    description: Published upstream release tag.
    required: true

runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - name: Validate dispatch target
      id: target
      shell: bash
      env:
        TAP_REPOSITORY: ${{ inputs.tap-repository }}
        TOOL: ${{ inputs.tool }}
        RELEASE_TAG: ${{ inputs.release-tag }}
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        if [[ ! "$TAP_REPOSITORY" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9-]+/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]]; then
          echo 'Expected tap-repository as owner/repository' >&2
          exit 1
        fi
        if [[ ! "$TOOL" =~ ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$ ]]; then
          echo 'Invalid tap tool name' >&2
          exit 1
        fi
        if [[ ! "$RELEASE_TAG" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._@+/-]{0,127}$ ]]; then
          echo 'Invalid release tag' >&2
          exit 1
        fi
        echo "owner=${TAP_REPOSITORY%%/*}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
        echo "repository=${TAP_REPOSITORY#*/}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    - name: Create tap-scoped token
      id: app-token
      uses: actions/create-github-app-token@64ab729a6294000f5aa4a4bc0b73d1f32bc45510 # v3
      with:
        client-id: ${{ inputs.client-id }}
        private-key: ${{ inputs.private-key }}
        owner: ${{ steps.target.outputs.owner }}
        repositories: ${{ steps.target.outputs.repository }}
        permission-contents: write
    - name: Dispatch release
      shell: bash
      env:
        GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
        TAP_REPOSITORY: ${{ inputs.tap-repository }}
        TOOL: ${{ inputs.tool }}
        RELEASE_TAG: ${{ inputs.release-tag }}
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        gh api "repos/${TAP_REPOSITORY}/dispatches" -f event_type=tool_released -f "client_payload[tool]=${TOOL}" -f "client_payload[tag]=${RELEASE_TAG}"

| Action | Use it when… | It does… |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`setup-rust`](setup-rust/action.yml) | A job needs a pinned Rust toolchain or cross target. | Installs Rust components and targets, then caches the build. |
| [`setup-proto-node-pnpm`](setup-proto-node-pnpm/action.yml) | A repo pins Node and pnpm in `.prototools`. | Installs both with proto and optionally caches the pnpm store. |
| [`setup-pnpm-cache`](setup-pnpm-cache/action.yml) | Node and pnpm are already installed. | Caches the pnpm store only. |
| [`notify-homebrew-tap`](notify-homebrew-tap/action.yml) | A trusted release job has published a CLI. | Sends its tool name and tag to the [Orin DX tap](https://github.com/orin-dx/homebrew-tap). |

Use a **reviewed, full commit SHA** in each caller. A moving tag or branch can change code that runs in a job with release credentials without a change in the calling repo.

## Set up a job

```yaml
steps:
  - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@<reviewed-full-commit-sha>
    with:
      toolchain: '1.96.0'
      components: 'clippy,rustfmt'
      targets: 'wasm32-wasip1'

  - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-proto-node-pnpm@<reviewed-full-commit-sha>
    with:
      working-directory: packages/my-node-package
```

`setup-proto-node-pnpm` reads the calling repository's `.prototools`; it does not install Rust. Use `setup-rust` alongside it when the job also needs a specific Rust target.

## Notify the Homebrew tap

Call this only after a trusted release workflow confirms publication from its receipt. The action sends **only a tool name and release tag**. The tap fetches the published archives, checks their digests and contents, and opens a formula PR for review.

```yaml
- uses: orin-dx/actions/notify-homebrew-tap@<reviewed-full-commit-sha>
  with:
    client-id: ${{ vars.TAP_APP_CLIENT_ID }}
    private-key: ${{ secrets.TAP_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
    tap-repository: orin-dx/homebrew-tap
    tool: callisto
    release-tag: ${{ steps.release.outputs.tag }}
```

The same action works for Caliper with `tool: caliper`; a future tool supplies its own name and tag. The GitHub App is installed only on the tap, and its secret is visible only to the tap and publishing repositories. The [tap automation guide](https://github.com/orin-dx/homebrew-tap/blob/main/docs/automation.md) has the one-time setup and trust boundaries.

## Work on these actions

See [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) for validation and caller checks, or [Security](SECURITY.md) to report a credential or workflow issue privately. The `main` branch and current pinned SHAs receive fixes; callers choose when to move to a newer reviewed SHA.

content.text:
The publish run failed, and it exposed two problems with how the first publish was set up.

**1. It failed because #5 was already merged.** `brew pr-pull` works by cherry-picking the PR's commits onto `main`, then adding the bottle commit. Merging with GitHub's button had already put those changes on `main`, so every cherry-pick came out empty and it stopped. The intended flow is to approve the PR and run `brew pr-pull` instead of pressing merge. It adds the bottle commit and closes the PR itself.

**2. The next failure is likely the ruleset.** `pr-pull` pushes straight to `main`, but the ruleset requires a PR. The only bypass today is org admins, via PR only. So even a correctly timed publish would probably be rejected at the push step. I haven't tested that, because we never got that far.

**Recovery for the first bottles.** We need a new open PR whose CI builds the formulae. It could be a trivial formula change or the next real version bump. Run `brew pr-pull` on that PR instead of merging it. CONTRIBUTING and `docs/automation.md` already say to run the publish workflow after approval. I'd make that explicit with "don't use the merge button".

**The ruleset decision is yours**, because it weakens a protection on `main`. The options are:
- **A.** Add a bypass for the publish identity: either the GitHub App, or the `github-actions` integration. Docs currently promise that the App can't bypass the ruleset, so those would need rewording. A narrower choice is a separate App used only by `publish.yml`.
- **B.** Run `brew pr-pull` locally as an admin, using your existing PR-only bypass. It needs no ruleset change and no new credential, but it's a manual step on your machine.

Yes, and moving to on-merge is better. Homebrew supports it directly: `brew pr-pull --no-cherry-pick` skips replaying the PR's commits, assumes they're already on `main`, and still downloads the PR's CI bottles, writes the bottle block, and uploads. That is exactly what failed on #5.

**Proposed flow**
1. You approve and merge the bump PR with the normal button.
2. A `pull_request_target: closed` trigger in `publish.yml` fires when the PR was merged. It's limited to Formula changes from branches in this repo, so fork PRs can't feed it artifacts.
3. It runs `brew pr-pull --no-cherry-pick <PR>`, then pushes the bottle commit to `main`.
4. Nothing to remember. The manual dispatch stays as a retry button.

**Why on-merge over on-approval**
- **No race.** An approval can arrive before CI finishes, and `pr-pull` needs finished, successful bottle artifacts. A merge can't happen until the required checks pass.
- **Natural for you.** Merging is the action you already take.

**Costs to accept**
- **Brief gap.** Between merge and the bottle commit (a few minutes), `main` has the new version without bottles. Installs in that window build from source.
- **Failure is quiet.** If the publish step fails, `main` stays unbottled. A failed run emails the person who merged, and the dispatch lets you re-run it.

**The ruleset still blocks the push.** The bottle commit goes straight to `main`, which requires a PR, so it needs a bypass. Options:
- **The existing GitHub App**, which would contradict the current docs ("cannot bypass the ruleset"), or a dedicated publish-only App.
- **The `github-actions` integration.** I believe it can be added as a bypass actor, but I haven't checked.

Either way, a compromised publish workflow could push to `main`. That's why it's restricted to merged, same-repo, Formula-only PRs, and runs base-branch workflow code.

**This also fixes the first bottles.** Once the bypass exists, I can dispatch the workflow for #5 with `--no-cherry-pick`. Its CI artifacts should still be available, so no follow-up PR is needed.

The `github-actions` integration can't be a bypass actor on this repo. I tested it against the API with a disabled throwaway ruleset (since deleted, so there's nothing left behind) and got:

> `422 Validation Failed: Actor GitHub Actions integration must be part of the ruleset source or owner organization`

The `GITHUB_TOKEN` identity isn't an App that our org owns or installed, so rulesets won't accept it. The web results agreed that the built-in token generally can't be a bypass actor, apart from one unverified claim to the contrary ([GitHub community discussion](https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/25305)).

That leaves a GitHub App, which does work as a bypass actor. I'd use a **dedicated publish App** instead of the existing updater App:
- **Isolated:** the existing App's key is used by the bump workflow, and a bypass on that App would let the bump workflow push to `main` too. A separate App limits the bypass to publishing.
- **Key kept out of other workflows:** store its key in a GitHub Environment named `publish`, restricted to the `main` branch. `pull_request_target: closed` runs the base branch's workflow code, so merged-PR publishing satisfies that restriction, and no PR branch can read the key.
- **Narrow permissions:** Contents write and Pull requests write, installed on `orin-dx/homebrew-tap` only.

**What you'd do (org admin):**
1. Create an App such as `orin-dx-homebrew-publisher` with webhooks off, and install it on the tap only.
2. Add it to the `main` ruleset's bypass list with mode **Always**.
3. Create the `publish` environment in the tap (deployment branches: `main` only), and add `PUBLISH_APP_CLIENT_ID` (variable) and `PUBLISH_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` (secret) to it.

**What I'd do:** update `publish.yml` to
- trigger on merged Formula PRs from this repo, plus a manual dispatch for retries;
- use the `publish` environment and mint a token with `actions/create-github-app-token`;
- run `brew pr-pull --no-cherry-pick`;
- update the docs (including the line saying the App can't bypass the ruleset), and then publish bottles for #5.

Yes, but it lands changes through a PR, so it doesn't change the constraint.

Callisto's release workflow never pushes to a protected branch directly. It opens a release PR (`callisto/version-packages`, via its `callisto-action`) with the token it already has. When you merge that PR, the push to `main` triggers the actual release, which creates tags and publishes. Tags aren't covered by the branch ruleset, so Callisto doesn't need a bypass anywhere.

The tap has the same shape up to the merge: the bump PR plays the part of Callisto's release PR. The difference is the last write. Homebrew's bottle model requires a commit on `main` after the bottles exist, because the bottle checksums go in the formula's `bottle do` block. That one commit is the only direct-to-`main` write we need.

There are three ways to land it:

1. **Dedicated publish App with a bypass.** This is how homebrew-core works: a bot with bypass runs `pr-pull`. It's the least friction, with nothing for you to do after merging. The cost is a second App and a bypass on `main`, scoped by the `publish` environment I described.
2. **Callisto-style bottles PR.** After you merge, the publish step uploads bottles and opens a follow-up PR with the `bottle do` change, which CI checks and you approve. No bypass is needed, but every release now takes two merges, which is the kind of step you said you'd forget. Auto-merge could shorten it. It would still require the approval the ruleset demands.
3. **Bottle block committed in the bump PR before merge.** The merge itself then carries the bottles, with no post-merge write. Homebrew has no supported flow for this, so it would be custom code and bottles would upload before review. I'd avoid it.

I'd still pick option 1. It matches Homebrew's own practice, and it keeps the manual work to a single merge click. Option 2 is the choice if you don't want any bypass on `main`.

# Based on the workflow brew tap-new generates. Bottles are published after a formula PR merges, not before:
# `--no-cherry-pick` tells brew pr-pull the PR's commits are already on main, so it only downloads the PR's
# test-bot bottles, uploads them, and adds the bottle commit.
name: brew pr-pull

on:
  # Runs the workflow from the base branch, so a PR cannot change what runs with the App token.
  pull_request_target:
    types: [closed]
    paths:
      - Formula/**
  # Retry for a merged PR whose publish run failed.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      pull_request:
        description: Merged pull request number
        required: true
      head_sha:
        description: Expected pull request head commit SHA (optional)

permissions: {}

defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash -xeuo pipefail {0}

concurrency:
  group: publish-bottles
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  pr-pull:
    # Only merged PRs from branches in this repository: their bottles were built by our own CI.
    if: >-
      github.repository == 'orin-dx/homebrew-tap' &&
      (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
       (github.event.pull_request.merged == true &&
        github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository))
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      actions: read
      attestations: write
      checks: read
      contents: read
      id-token: write
      issues: read
      pull-requests: read
    steps:
      # The App is on the main ruleset's bypass list, so it can push the bottle commit without a PR.
      - name: Create tap-scoped GitHub App token
        id: app-token
        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@64ab729a6294000f5aa4a4bc0b73d1f32bc45510 # v3
        with:
          client-id: ${{ vars.TAP_APP_CLIENT_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.TAP_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          owner: orin-dx
          repositories: homebrew-tap
          permission-contents: write
          permission-pull-requests: write

      - name: Set up Homebrew
        uses: Homebrew/actions/setup-homebrew@4790763c0a3ba4036f72634dc079c4a7dfcd4878 # 2026.10.19.1
        with:
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}

      - name: Set up git
        id: git_setup
        uses: Homebrew/actions/git-user-config@4790763c0a3ba4036f72634dc079c4a7dfcd4878 # 2026.10.19.1

      - name: Pull bottles
        id: pull_bottles
        env:
          HOMEBREW_GITHUB_API_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
          HOMEBREW_GIT_COMMITTER_NAME: ${{ steps.git_setup.outputs.name }}
          HOMEBREW_GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL: ${{ steps.git_setup.outputs.email }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ inputs.head_sha || github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          PULL_REQUEST: ${{ inputs.pull_request || github.event.pull_request.number }}
        run: |
          if [[ -n "$HEAD_SHA" ]]
          then
            brew pr-pull --debug --retain-bottle-dir --no-cherry-pick --tap="$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
              --head-sha="$HEAD_SHA" "$PULL_REQUEST"
          else
            brew pr-pull --debug --retain-bottle-dir --no-cherry-pick --tap="$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" "$PULL_REQUEST"
          fi

      - name: Generate build provenance
        uses: actions/attest@1e69f48acb82d1966a394da916b4c1698aa569d6 # v4.2.2
        with:
          subject-path: "${{ steps.pull_bottles.outputs.bottle_path }}/*.tar.gz"

      - name: Push commits
        uses: Homebrew/actions/git-try-push@4790763c0a3ba4036f72634dc079c4a7dfcd4878 # 2026.10.19.1
        with:
          branch: main

content.text:
[PR #7](https://github.com/orin-dx/homebrew-tap/pull/7) is open with the on-merge publish workflow, and the bypass is confirmed on the ruleset. The workflow has not actually run yet.

**What it does.** When a formula PR from this repo merges, `publish.yml` runs `brew pr-pull --no-cherry-pick`. That downloads the PR's CI bottles, uploads them, and pushes the bottle commit to `main` as the updater App. It runs from the base branch only, and the dispatch stays as a retry. The docs now describe the bypass and its trust boundary. `brew style`, including actionlint, passes on the workflow.

**Bypass.**
- The updater App is now on the ruleset list with **Always allow**, which is what the workflow needs.
- The list also has **Repository admin** and your user, both with always-allow. Those let any repo admin push to `main` directly. If you only meant to add the App, you may want to remove them.
- The bypass isn't limited to the bottle commit. Any workflow that can mint the App token could push to `main`, so I wrote that into `SECURITY.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md` rather than claiming the App can't.

**What's unverified.** CI on #7 will lint and check it, but the publish step has never run end to end. Whether `--no-cherry-pick` works on a PR that is already merged, and whether the upload to GitHub Packages is permitted, will only show up in the first real run.

**Next steps.**
1. Approve and merge #7.
2. I re-run the publish dispatch for #5 to publish its bottles. Say when you're ready.

content.text: Applying the fix: compute the commit before the merge, run `pr-pull` with that as `GITHUB_SHA`, and add `--clean`.

input.new_string:
# brew pr-pull finds the formulae that need bottles by diffing from the merge-base of origin/HEAD and
      # GITHUB_SHA to HEAD. On main after a squash merge that diff is empty unless GITHUB_SHA is the commit
      # the PR merged onto.
      - name: Find the commit before the merge
        id: base
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
          PULL_REQUEST: ${{ inputs.pull_request || github.event.pull_request.number }}
        run: |
          merge_sha=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/pulls/$PULL_REQUEST" --jq .merge_commit_sha)
          [[ -n "$merge_sha" && "$merge_sha" != null ]] || { echo "Pull request $PULL_REQUEST is not merged" >&2; exit 1; }
          base_sha=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$merge_sha" --jq '.parents[0].sha')
          echo "sha=$base_sha" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Pull bottles
        id: pull_bottles
        env:
          HOMEBREW_GITHUB_API_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
          HOMEBREW_GIT_COMMITTER_NAME: ${{ steps.git_setup.outputs.name }}
          HOMEBREW_GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL: ${{ steps.git_setup.outputs.email }}
          BASE_SHA: ${{ steps.base.outputs.sha }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ inputs.head_sha || github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          PULL_REQUEST: ${{ inputs.pull_request || github.event.pull_request.number }}
        run: |
          # --clean keeps brew from amending the commit that is already on main.

content.text:
The first publish attempt for #5 failed, and I have a fix in [PR #8](https://github.com/orin-dx/homebrew-tap/pull/8). It isn't verified end to end yet. It's open for you to merge; then I'll re-run the publish for #5.

**Why it failed.** The ruleset bypass worked, and the run got past the push. The failure was in `brew pr-pull --no-cherry-pick`. It finds formulae needing bottles by diffing from the merge-base to `HEAD`, and that diff is empty on `main` after a squash merge. It skipped the artifacts, then the attestation step failed because no tarballs existed.

**The fix.**
- Run it with `GITHUB_SHA` set to the commit the PR merged onto.
- Add `--clean`, so Homebrew doesn't amend the commit already on `main`.
- It assumes squash or merge-commit merges. A rebase merge would need a different base.

**Docs.** Bottles are hosted on this repo's GitHub Releases, not GitHub Packages. I checked the bottle JSON from CI, which uses `github.com/orin-dx/homebrew-tap/releases/download/...`. The docs now say that and that no package permissions are needed.

**A separate problem: #5's CI bottles are incomplete.**
- **Bottles built:** `caliper` and `callisto@0.14` on macOS ARM, Linux ARM and Linux x86-64.
- **`callisto` 0.15.0:** not bottled. On the runner, `callisto@0.14` ended up symlinked into the Homebrew prefix, so `callisto` couldn't link over it. I don't know why a keg-only formula was linked. The job still reported success.
- **macOS Intel:** all four jobs passed, but there is no artifact for it, so no Intel macOS bottle exists.

Re-running the publish for #5 would give bottles for `caliper` and `callisto@0.14` only. `callisto` would still build from source until a later PR rebuilds it.

**Next steps.**
1. Merge #8. I'll then re-run the publish for #5 to test the fix.
2. Decide whether I should chase the `callisto` linking conflict and the missing Intel bottles now. The conflict will recur on every release that snapshots a versioned formula alongside the main one.

content.text:
Yes, there are changes. The "build at install" assumption doesn't hold on Intel Macs, so I'd rework #9 before it merges.

**What the Intel CI job actually did.** It didn't test anything. For `callisto@0.14`, `caliper` and `callisto`, `test-bot` printed `SKIPPED ... has dependencies without compatible bottles: rust`. That's why the job took 7 minutes against 16 to 19 for the others, and why it passed without producing a bottle. The required `macOS Intel` check is effectively a no-op.

**What that means for Intel users.** Homebrew has no `rust` bottle for that platform, so `rust` is a build dependency with no bottle there. An install on an Intel Mac would compile Rust (and LLVM) from source before it even builds callisto or caliper. That is likely hours, not the few minutes I implied. So "builds at install" is closer to "effectively unsupported" for Intel.

**Changes I'd make**
1. **Drop the Intel job** from `tests.yml`, since it verifies nothing. Remove `macOS Intel` from the ruleset's required checks in the same step, or the PR will wait forever on a check that no longer exists, as happened before.
2. **Reword #9.** Say Intel Macs aren't supported, and that an install would compile the Rust toolchain from source. I'd remove "old enough that building is fine".
3. **Optional:** add `depends_on arch: :arm64`, or `on_intel { odie ... }` hmm, a stronger option is to make the formula fail fast on Intel macOS with a clear message, instead of letting users start a multi-hour build. I'd lean towards that. It's a few lines in each formula, and it also needs a bottle rebuild.

The alternative is to keep Intel usable, which means shipping a prebuilt binary for it again. That's the custom machinery we removed, so I wouldn't.

How do you want to handle Intel macOS: unsupported with a clear failure message, or just documented as slow? Once you choose, I'll do the CI change, update #9, and give you the ruleset edit to make, since I'd rather not change the required checks without your say-so.

Homebrew itself no longer publishes Intel macOS bottles, which is why this isn't specific to our tap. The `oxlint` formula I pulled earlier from homebrew-core lists bottles only for `arm64_golden_gate`, `arm64_tahoe`, `arm64_sequoia`, `arm64_linux` and `x86_64_linux`, with no Intel macOS entry. The `rust` formula reports a single bottle platform here as well. So on an Intel Mac, `rust` (and `llvm`, which it depends on) has to be compiled before a Rust formula can build.

I haven't timed that build. "Multi-hour" is my guess from how large those two builds are, so treat it as "long, and not minutes". My earlier "a few minutes" was also wrong for Intel. It holds on the platforms with bottles, where only callisto or caliper compiles.

So this is a Homebrew-wide limitation, and any Rust CLI in any tap has it on Intel Macs. That doesn't make it fine for our users, but it does change the call:
- **Unsupported, with a clear message:** the formulae fail fast on Intel macOS, which also lets us drop the Intel CI job.
- **Documented only:** Intel installs work but are very slow, and the docs say so.
- **Prebuilt binary for Intel:** this brings back custom machinery, so I wouldn't.

My recommendation is the first. A fast failure with a clear message beats someone starting a multi-hour build. Which one do you want? Then I'll update #9, drop the Intel job, and give you the ruleset edit.
